- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to align with recent downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment turns neutral.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply mean reversion to recent 7–10 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to dampen noise.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if no clear reversal signal.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a steeper decline than actual; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment remains negative for 3+ days.
